questions.html: For a set of $n$ integers in arithmetic progression, the difference between twice the median of the set and the range of the set is equal to twice the first term.
questions.solution:
Answer: Not available

Source solution 1 (score: 0)

$$
\text { Median }=\frac{\text { First }+ \text { Last }}{2} \Longrightarrow 2 \times \text { Median }=\text { First }+ \text { Last }
$$

Range: By definition, $\text{Range $=$ Last - First.}$

The Equation:
$$
\begin{gathered}
\text { Difference }=(2 \times \text { Median })-\text { Range } \\
\text { Difference }=(\text { First }+ \text { Last })-(\text { Last }- \text { First }) \\
\text { Difference }=2 \times \text { First }
\end{gathered}
$$

questions.html: If the median of a set consisting of $n$ consecutive odd positive integers is an even integer, the sum of the mean and the range of the set is an odd integer.
questions.solution:
Answer: Not available

Source solution 1 (score: 0)

  • Mean: In a symmetric set, Mean = Median = Even.

 

  • Range: For $n$ consecutive odd integers, Range $=2(n-1)$ which is always Even.


The Sum:
$$
\text { Mean }+ \text { Range }=\text { Even }+ \text { Even }=\text { Even }
$$

Since the sum is always even, it can never be an odd integer.

questions.html: In a class, $25 \%$ of the students get a scholarship. There are $40$ girls and $50 \%$ of them get a scholarship. If the girls constitute $25 \%$ of the strength of the class, then find the percentage of boys who get a scholarship.
questions.solution:
Answer: Not available

Source solution 1 (score: 0)

Total Class Strength: Since girls constitute $25 \%\left(\frac{1}{4}\right)$ of the class:
$$
\text { Total Students }=40 \times 4=160
$$

Boys: Total - Girls = $160-40=120$

Total Scholarships: $25 \%$ of total students $=\frac{1}{4} \times 160=40$

Girls with Scholarship: $50 \%$ of girls $=\frac{1}{2} \times 40=20$

Boys with Scholarship: Total Scholarships - Girls Scholarships $=40-20 = 20$

Percentage of boys with a scholarship = $\left(\frac{20 \text { boys with scholarship }}{120 \text { total boys }}\right) \times 100=\frac{1}{6} \times 100=16.66 \%$

questions.html: Ankita and Varun are $150$ m apart and facing towards each other. Ankita took a left turn and walked $30$ m , while Varun also took a left turn and walked $50$ m. Ankita then took two consecutive right turns walking $70$ m in each turn. Meanwhile Varun took a right turn and stopped after walking $40$ m . If Varun is now facing towards West direction, then how far and in which direction is Ankita now with respect to Varun?
questions.solution:
Answer: Not available

Source solution 1 (score: 0)

$\textbf{1. Coordinates}$

  • Ankita's final position: $(70,-40)$
  • Varun's final position: $(110,-50)$


$\textbf{2. Relative Differences}$

  •  $\Delta x$ (Horizontal): $70-110=-40 \mathrm{~m}$ (West)
  • $\Delta y$ (Vertical): $-40-(-50)=+10 \mathrm{~m}$ (North)


$\textbf{3. Calculation}$

  • Distance: $\sqrt{(-40)^{2}+(10)^{2}}=\sqrt{1700}=10 \sqrt{17} \mathrm{~m}$
  • Direction: Since she is North and West of Varun, the direction is North-West.

questions.html: Raghav buys a shop for  $120000$. He pays half of the amount in cash and agrees to pay the balance in $12$ annual installments of  $5000$ each. If the rate of interest is $12 \%$ and he pays with the installment the interest due on the unpaid amount, then find the total cost of the shop.
questions.solution:
Answer: Not available

Source solution 1 (score: 0)

Total Value: $1,20,000$

Cash Paid: $\frac{1}{2} \times 1,20,000= 60,000$

Unpaid Balance: $60,000$ (Paid in $12$ installments of $5,000$ each)

Interest is calculated annually at $12 \%$ on the remaining unpaid amount:

  • Year $1$ Interest: $12\%$ of $60,000 = 7,200$
  • Year $2$ Interest: $12 \%$ of $55,000=6,600$
  • Year $12$ Interest: $12\%$ of $5,000 =600$


This forms an AP series: $7200,6600, \ldots, 600$ with $n=12$ terms.
$$
\text { Total Interest }=\frac{n}{2} \times(\text { First term }+ \text { Last term })
$$

Total Interest $=\frac{12}{2} \times(7200+600)=6 \times 7800= 46,800$ 

Total Cost $=$ Original Value + Total Interest

Total Cost $=1,20,000+46,800=1,66,800$
